title: Other Elasticities: PES, YED, XED

final_note: Different elasticities answer different strategic questions.

concepts.def: Percent change in quantity supplied / percent change in price.
Percent change in quantity demanded / percent change in income.
Percent change in demand for A / percent change in price of B.
XED greater than 0; complements have XED less than 0.

walkthroughs.body_html: PES is higher when firms have spare capacity, mobile inputs and long time horizons. Agriculture is short-run inelastic - harvests take time.
YED greater than 1 marks luxuries (foreign holidays); 0 to 1 marks normal goods (bread); negative marks inferiors (instant noodles). Predicts which sectors boom in growth and shrink in recession.

XED reveals substitutes and complements. Strong negative XED between razors and razor blades; strong positive between Pepsi and Coke. Marketers use these to design bundles and counter rival promotions.

Strong substitutes
Independent
Inferior
A luxury good
An inferior good
A normal good

mcqs.q: What does Income Elasticity of Demand (YED) tell us?
options: PED measures whether a product is expensive or cheap.
A negative YED means the demand calculation went wrong.
The sign tells us the good type: positive YED = normal good (rises with income); negative YED = inferior good (falls with income). YED > 1 indicates a luxury; YED between 0 and 1 a necessity.
YED measures how the rich and poor differ in tastes.

mcqs.q: How does the sign of cross elasticity of demand (XED) reveal product relationships?
options: YED measures how the rich and poor differ in tastes.
Positive XED = substitutes (price of one rises, demand for the other rises); negative XED = complements (price of one rises, demand for the other falls); zero XED = unrelated goods.
The sign of XED doesn't matter — only the size does.
XED measures how often consumers cross-shop between stores.

mcqs.q: What does price elasticity of demand measure?
options: PED measures whether a product is expensive or cheap.
XED measures how often consumers cross-shop between stores.
PED measures how flexible or stretchy a product is.
The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price — the percentage change in quantity divided by the percentage change in price.
